Plant the Moon Jr. Challenge Final Report 
How Different Colors of Light Affect Plant Growth” 
Team Name: NPSA 2- Apollos 
Team Photo:
  
  
Independent Variable: Color of Light Used: Purple, Blue, White, Natural (control)  
Dependent Variable: Plant height (cm) - Number of leaves - Leaf color - Time to 
germination - Overall plant health  
Controls/Constants: Natural light, - Plant species - Soil type and composition - Watering 
schedule - Temperature and humidity - Pot size and planting depth - Duration of light 
exposure  
Hypothesis: Plants grown under blue light will show the most leaf development, while 
red light will promote height, and white light will produce balanced growth.  
Background/Reasoning: We chose the Moon experiment category because lunar 
exploration requires sustainable food production for future missions. Understanding how 
plants respond to different light conditions is critical since natural sunlight on the Moon 
is limited, and artificial lighting will likely be necessary in lunar habitats.  
Our independent variable is the color of light used (Red, Blue, White, Natural), as light 
spectrum significantly influences plant growth and development. Different wavelengths 
affect photosynthesis and plant morphology in unique ways, making this an essential 
factor for controlled lunar agriculture.  
The dependent variables—plant height, number of leaves, leaf color, time to germination, 
and overall plant health—were selected because they provide measurable indicators of 
growth performance and vitality under varying light conditions. These metrics help 
determine which light spectrum best supports healthy plant development in a simulated 
lunar environment.

By controlling factors such as soil type, watering schedule, temperature, and pot size, we 
ensure that any differences observed are due to light color alone. This approach allows us to 
test our hypothesis: Blue light will promote leaf development, red light will encourage 
height, and white light will provide balanced growth.  
  
Experimental Rational: Our experiment provides valuable insights into optimizing plant 
growth under artificial lighting, which is essential for future lunar missions. Since natural 
sunlight on the Moon is limited and inconsistent, astronauts will rely on controlled environments 
with artificial light to grow food. Understanding how different light wavelengths affect plant 
height, leaf development, germination time, and overall health helps identify the most efficient 
lighting strategies for sustainable lunar agriculture.  
By testing red, blue, and white light against natural light, we contribute data that can guide the 
design of lunar greenhouses and life-support systems. This research not only supports space 
exploration but also advances knowledge in controlled-environment agriculture on Earth, where 
similar techniques are used in vertical farming and resource-limited settings.

Procedures:   
Step 1: Set Up  
●​ Get 16 small pots with the same soil and seeds.  
●​ Put 1–2 seeds in each pot at the same depth.  
●​ Make 4 groups:   
o​
Purple light (4 pots)  
o​
Blue light (4 pots)  
o​
White light (4 pots)  
o​
Natural light (4 pots) – this is our control.  
●​ Put each group under its light. Keep them in the same room so the temperature is the 
same.  
●​ Label each pot so you know which group it belongs to.  
Step 2: Light and Water  
●​ Red, blue, and white lights stay on for 12 hours every day, then off for 12 hours.  
●​ Natural light group gets sunlight from the window.  
●​ Water all pots on the same days with the same amount of water.  
Step 3: Watch and Measure  
●​ Check every day to see when seeds sprout. Write down the day they sprout.  
●​ Every two days, measure:   
o​
Height (use a ruler)  
o​
Number of leaves  
o​
Leaf color (green, light green, or yellow)  
o​
How healthy the plant looks (strong or weak)  
●​ Take a picture of each pot every time you measure.  
Step 4: Keep It Fair  
●​ Same soil, same seeds, same pot size, same water, same light time.  
●​ Rotate pots in each group every two days so no pot gets a “better spot.”

Analysis: 
1) Growth (Height)  
●​ Purple ended tallest (20 cm) and took the lead from Week 4 onward.  
●​ White grew the fastest on average, with the largest total growth (16 cm) and steady gains 
early.  
●​ Blue grew steadily to 15 cm, trailing White and Purple in final height.  
●​ Natural light grew the least and plateaued around 10 cm by Week 6–8.  
2) Leaf Development  
●​ All artificial lights (Purple, Blue, White) reached 7 leaves by Week 4 and stayed there.  
●​ Natural light reached only 3 leaves by Week 4 and never increased after that.  
3) Leaf & Stem Color Notes  
●​ Purple light: leaves described as green + red, with a purple stem throughout.  
●​ White light: green/pink leaves; stem notes blank (likely normal/unchanged).  
●​ Blue light: green leaves; pink stem starting Week 4.  
●​ Natural light: green leaves; no color changes noted.  
These color differences suggest that different light colors change plant pigments, especially in 
stems (pink/purple) and leaves (green + pink/red). That’s useful for understanding plant 
responses to light spectrums.  
  
Future Considerations:  
If we repeat this experiment, we would make these improvements:  
1.​ Test More Light Colors  
a.​ Add pure red light and maybe green light to see how they compare to purple, blue, and 
white.  
2.​ Use More Plants  
a.​ Grow more pots in each group to make results more accurate.  
3.​ Measure More Things  
a.​ Check stem thickness, root growth, and flowering time, not just height and leaves.  
4.​ Track Water and Temperature  
a.​ Record soil moisture and room temperature every day to see if they affect growth.  
5.​ Try Different Plants  
a.​ Test other species to see if the results are the same or different.

Conclusion: This season, we learned that light color makes a big difference in how plants grow. 
All plants under artificial lights grew much better than the ones in natural light. Purple light gave 
us the tallest plants, white light grew fast and steady, and blue light grew healthy plants but a 
little shorter. Natural light plants grew the slowest and stopped growing early.  
  
The coolest thing we discovered was that different lights changed the plant colors! Purple light 
made stems turn purple, blue light made stems pink, and white light gave leaves a pink tint. This 
shows that plants respond to light in amazing ways, which is important for growing food on the 
Moon.
